column3:
Customers need an optional phone number.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer has an optional phone field (string, max 30 chars)
- POST and PUT accept phone; GET returns it (null when not set)
- A phone longer than 30 chars returns 422
- Existing tests still pass

Implement create, read, update, delete and list for products, mirroring services/customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Product fields: id, sku (unique), name, description (optional), price (decimal, > 0), created_at, updated_at
- Endpoints: POST /products, GET /products, GET /products/{id}, PUT /products/{id}, DELETE /products/{id}
- Duplicate sku returns 409; missing product returns 404; price <= 0 returns 422
- Tests cover every endpoint and every error case above

Implement orders in services/orders. No cross-service validation yet (that is RETAIL-4).

Acceptance criteria:
- Order fields: id, customer_id, status (pending | confirmed | cancelled, default pending), created_at, updated_at
- An order has one or more line items: product_id, quantity (>= 1), unit_price (> 0)
- Endpoints: POST /orders, GET /orders, GET /orders/{id}, PUT /orders/{id}, DELETE /orders/{id}
- An order with zero line items returns 422
- Tests cover every endpoint and error case

column1: Validate customer and products when creating an order
column3:
Orders must reference real customers and products. Call the customers and products services over HTTP using CUSTOMERS_URL and PRODUCTS_URL.

Acceptance criteria:
- POST and PUT /orders return 422 with a clear message if the customer does not exist
- POST and PUT /orders return 422 naming the missing product_id(s) if any product does not exist
- If a dependent service is unreachable, return 503
- HTTP calls are mocked in tests; no test needs other services running
- Depends on RETAIL-2 and RETAIL-3

column1: Add pagination to all list endpoints
column3:
List endpoints currently return everything.

Acceptance criteria:
- GET /customers, /products and /orders accept limit (default 50, max 200) and offset (default 0)
- limit outside 1..200 or negative offset returns 422
- Behaviour is identical across all three services
- Each service has tests for defaults, custom values and invalid values

Support finding a customer by email.

Acceptance criteria:
- GET /customers?email=<address> returns a list containing only the matching customer, or an empty list
- Matching is case-insensitive
- Tests cover match, no match and mixed case

Clients need the order total without summing line items themselves.

Acceptance criteria:
- Order responses include total = sum(quantity * unit_price) across line items
- total is computed, not stored
- Tests cover single and multiple line items
- Depends on RETAIL-3

column1: Handle deleting a customer who has orders
column3:
Today a customer can be deleted even if they have orders. Decide and implement the right behaviour.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deleting a customer who has orders must not leave the system in an inconsistent state
- Behaviour is documented in the PR

column1: Coding style guide and readability refactor
column3:
Code should be easy to read for developers who are not Python experts, without losing quality or performance.

Acceptance criteria:
- style.md at the repo root defines the coding style, with examples from this codebase
- CLAUDE.md requires all code to follow style.md and adds it to the definition of done
- services/customers (app and tests) follows style.md, with no change in API behaviour
- Create and update copy fields explicitly, with a comment showing the shorter Python alternative
- Guard tests fail if a field is added to the schemas but not copied by create or update
- The products and orders scaffolds follow style.md
- All existing tests still pass

column1: Block deleting a product that orders refer to
column3:
Today a product can be deleted even when orders refer to it (deferred from RETAIL-2). Products must ask the orders service before deleting, over HTTP using an ORDERS_URL environment variable.

Acceptance criteria:
- DELETE /products/{id} returns 409 with a clear message if any order has a line item for that product_id
- DELETE /products/{id} still returns 204 when no order refers to the product, and 404 when the product does not exist
- If the orders service is unreachable, DELETE returns 503 and the product is not deleted
- The orders service exposes a way to find orders by product_id; document the contract in the PR
- HTTP calls are mocked in tests; no test needs other services running
- Depends on RETAIL-2 and RETAIL-3
